subject: Post-call: Performance/SLO & Autoscaling follow-up

Subject: Post-call: Performance/SLO & Autoscaling follow-up

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our Perf/SLO discussion so your team has everything in one place.

Call highlights / customer goals
- Primary SLOs: p50 latency <= 150ms, p95 <= 400ms for 1k concurrent streaming sessions.
- Throughput target: sustained 1k concurrent requests, peak bursts to 3k QPS for short windows.
- Streaming: server-sent streaming required for progressive token delivery; client needs first-token < 150ms and steady token delivery after that.

Autoscaling & warm-pool items we discussed
- Cold scale-up (spin-up new GPU instance): ~60–120s depending on instance type and image pull.
- Warm pool: recommended for your profile — warm pool reduces scale-up to ~8–20s because model is loaded in memory and containers are ready.
- Burst capacity: we can configure short-duration burst capacity (pre-reserved) to cover 3x sustained peaks; there is a cost tradeoff.
- Queueing behavior: Redwood can queue requests when capacity is constrained; however queueing adds to end-to-end latency and can cause SLO misses for p95. We recommend aggressive warm-pool sizing + client-side retry/backoff for best experience.

Action items / next steps
1) I’ll share a short tech note with warm-pool sizing recommendations and expected scale-up numbers (attached).
2) Rishi to propose an initial warm-pool sizing plan and perf test design to validate p95 under burst.
3) Schedule a 60-min deep-dive with your infra/plat eng team next week to review configuration and run a lightload perf test.

Attached: redwood_warmpool_sla.pdf (warm-pool recommendations), acme_autoscale_diagram.png (example topology).

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll coordinate Rishi and send the perf plan.

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- When you say 1k concurrent requests, is that concurrent streaming sessions or inference requests-per-second? Our traffic is session-based (long-ish streams).
- For first-token <150ms, is that assuming the model is in warm pool? What are numbers for a cold start (no warm pool)?
- For burst capacity, what typical billing model do you recommend — short pre-warm instances or pay-as-you-burst? We'd like to minimize steady-state cost.

Also, can Rishi call out any specific model size constraints? We're evaluating a 7B quantized model and a 13B float model for quality trade-offs.

Thanks — Daniel

Good questions — answered inline and looping in Rishi for model-specific numbers.

- 1k concurrent = 1k concurrent streaming sessions (long-lived connections). For steady-state throughput, that maps roughly to 150–250 tokens/sec aggregate depending on average tokens per request.
- First-token <150ms assumes warm pool + preloaded model and an optimized runtime; cold-start first-token is typically 600–1200ms depending on instance and model size (image pull + load + compile).
- Billing recommendations: for your usage pattern (sustained baseline with short spikes) we usually suggest a small reserved baseline (dedicated or reserved warm pool) plus dynamic burst capacity. That minimizes steady-state cost while ensuring SLOs for peaks. We can show numbers in the perf plan.
- Model size: Rishi will include expected memory footprints and estimated p50/p95 numbers for a 7B quantized vs 13B float model. Short version: quantized 7B will be ~2–3x faster and far cheaper to warm; 13B float gives quality improvements but increases memory and cold-start time.

Rishi — can you put together a recommended warm-pool size for the 1k concurrent baseline and a perf test scenario to validate p95 at 3k burst? Suggested timing: deep-dive Tuesday or Wednesday next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance/SLO & Autoscaling follow-up

Thanks Marissa — adding the perf/infra specifics below. Attaching a 1-page perf test plan (perf_test_plan.xlsx) and a small diagram.

Key numbers (approx) for Redwood runtime on NVIDIA A10 / A100 class instances:
- 7B quantized: memory ~12–16GB, p50 ~40–60ms, p95 ~120–180ms (warm). Cold-start: 45–90s to warm.
- 13B float: memory ~28–40GB, p50 ~90–140ms, p95 ~300–500ms (warm). Cold-start: 90–180s to warm.

Warm-pool sizing approach (initial recommendation for your 1k concurrent streaming sessions):
- Baseline warm pool: provision capacity for ~1k concurrent sessions mapped to ~12 warm workers (instance size depending on model; we’ll size per model in the plan).
- Burst buffer: keep an additional 8–16 pre-warmed instances for 1–5 minute bursts to cover 3k peak (mix of warm workers + short-lived spawn).
- Scale-up behavior: auto-scalers trigger new instances immediately but full readiness (model loaded + runtime compiled) is the gating event; plan for a 10–20s warm-pool warmup vs 60–120s cold.

Queueing & SLO interaction:
- If requests queue at the load-balancer while instances are cold, p95 will increase significantly — we recommend strict queue-time SLOs and early rejection + client retry with jitter for very latency-sensitive calls.

Perf test proposal (high-level)
1) Baseline: 1k concurrent streaming sessions for 30 minutes validating p50/p95.
2) Burst test: ramp to 3k over 30s, hold 2 minutes, observe p95 and error rates.
3) Cold-start test: drain warm pool and measure first-token latency for 10 requests.

I’ll upload the detailed perf plan and a sizing sheet to the Drive link Marissa shared. If you’re good with Tuesday 10/20 or Wednesday 10/21 for the deep-dive I’ll block time.
